content.title: RBC Heritage payouts for 2026 winner Matt Fitzpatrick, every golfer
content.text: Updated April 19, 2026, 8:04 p.m. ETAfter blowing his lead on the 18th hole, Matt Fitzpatrick held off world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler in a sudden-death playoff to come away with the win in the RBC Heritage at Harbour Town Golf Links in Hilton Head, South Carolina, on Sunday, April 19.Both golfers ended the tournament with identical 18-under-par scores before replaying the 18th hole in a playoff. Fitzpatrick nailed his second shot on the par-4 hole, leaving him a 13-foot birdie attempt, while Scheffler failed to reach the green with his fairway shot. The Englishman then knocked in the clutch birdie to capture his fourth career PGA Tour victory.Sunday marks the second win of 2026 for Fitzpatrick, who also won the RBC Heritage in 2023 and grew up vacationing at Harbour Town Golf Links with his family. He won the Valspar Championship on March 19 one week after finishing second in The Players Championship.Fitzpatrick had a 3-shot lead entering Sunday's final round and started fast with a with a 10-foot birdie putt on the first hole and a 17-foot birdie putt on No. 3 to stretch his lead to as many as four strokes.From there, though, things started to go south for the 2022 U.S. Open champion.Scheffler began to close as Fitzpatrick missed birdie opportunities in the second and fifth holes, though he sunk a crucial 20-foot putt on No. 11 to rescue par. Scheffler hit birdies on No. 15 and 16 to get within one shot of Fitzpatrick, who ended with a bogey on the 18th – his lone bogey of the day – after a botched chip shot followed by a missed putt for par that put Scheffler into a tie for the lead and forced sudden death.Here are the payouts for every golfer who made the cut at the RBC Heritage:RBC Heritage purse, payoutsThe RBC Heritage at Harbour Town Golf Links in Hilton Head Island, S.C. has a total purse of $20 million, including $3.6 million to the winner.
